title: On Desirable Semantics of Functional Dependencies over Databases with Incomplete Information
review_status: full-text audit complete; desiderata, vague/disjunctive-table models, PFD semantics, impossibility/NP-completeness results, indexed checking, and authors' acknowledged normative/future-work boundaries checked
sections_checked: Sections 5–6: semantic definitions and disjunctive-table impossibility
Section 7: weak-FD seamless-satisfaction NP-completeness and PFD checking
Conclusion/further research: axiom-set subjectivity and expressive-model gap
venue_year_verified: Fundamenta Informaticae 158(4), 2018, pp. 327–352; DOI 10.3233/FI-2018-1651; arXiv v2 2017-04-06
evidence_note: PFDs meet the stated desiderata on vague tables; no FD semantics can meet all of them on disjunctive tables. Weak-FD seamless satisfaction is NP-complete. PFD checking can be indexed by possible LHS valuations. The desiderata are motivated intuitively and the authors invite alternative/maximal sets, so the theorem is conditional on that selected property list.

title: Computing Optimal Repairs for Functional Dependencies
review_status: full-text audit complete; subset-repair dichotomy, APX-hardness, weighted/duplicate cases, MPD resolution, update-repair sufficient conditions/approximations and distinct unresolved classification checked
sections_checked: Abstract and distinction between optimal S-repair and U-repair
Section 3: polynomial/APX-complete S-repair dichotomy and general-FD MPD theorem
Section 4: U-repair reductions, opposite-complexity examples, approximations and open full dichotomy
Conclusion and the PODS/TODS publication history
evidence_note: Subset repairs admit a dichotomy across FD sets; hard cases are APX-complete, and the general-FD MPD dichotomy is resolved. Update repairs are not equivalent: some FD sets reverse subset-vs-update tractability; the paper supplies partial results but explicitly leaves a full U-repair dichotomy open.

title: Spatial Co-location Pattern Mining - A new perspective using Graph Database
review_status: full-text audit complete; clique/neighborhood graph model, Chicago data scope, Titan/Cassandra/MongoDB/Elastic setup, algorithm runtime/memory comparison, threshold-update timings, and future-work boundary checked; venue not verified
sections_checked: Three traversal algorithms and time/memory trade-offs
Section VI: Chicago data, graph/database components, thread count, N/R/PI tables
Conclusion: interactive-analysis claim and unimplemented directions
venue_year_verified: arXiv preprint v1 submitted 2018-10-21; no venue or DOI verified in arXiv metadata
evidence_note: Evaluation uses 30,000 Chicago crime incidents across 33 crime types, with graph size up to 30,000 and a 48-thread pool. At N=30,000 and R=0.3 km, CliqueExtend/CliqueEnumG/CliqueEnumK take 392/578/12,837 seconds. At N=20,000, updating threshold 0.4→0.5 km takes 111.4s vs 313.8s for fresh graph creation (about 2.8x). CliqueExtend uses more storage. This does not establish a general graph DB speedup or low-latency interaction.

title: Database Repairing with Soft Functional Dependencies
review_status: targeted follow-up; official ACM abstract and publication record checked for problem distinction, special-case algorithms and incomplete general classification; full text not audited in this batch
sections_checked: ACM abstract: soft-constraint objective and relation to cardinality repairs
ACM introduction/summary: special cases and open classification boundary
venue_year_verified: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 49(2), 2024; DOI 10.1145/3651156
evidence_note: Adjacent soft-FD objective rather than identical hard subset or cell-update repairs. The article gives general hardness/approximation results and algorithms for a single FD and bipartite matching; broad classification remains incomplete. It does not resolve the sampled paper's hard U-repair dichotomy.
